steps.text: Look for chest indrawing in all sick children. Pay special attention to children with cough or cold, or children who are having any difficult breathing.
Ask the caregiver to raise the child’s clothing above the chest. Look at the lower chest wall (lower ribs).
Look for chest indrawing when the child breathes IN. Normally when a child breathes IN, the chest and stomach move out together.

If you see chest indrawing only when the child is crying or feeding, the child does not have chest indrawing. If you are unsure whether the child has chest indrawing, look again. If other community health workers are available, ask what they see.
